text: Parfit's non-identity problem threatens person-affecting ethics because many large-scale policy choices:
choices: generate obligations to rectify injustices committed before the affected people were born.
require us to deny bivalence for statements about what future people will do.
affect which particular people will come to exist, not merely how well already-existing people will fare.
show that an indefinitely extended human future would eventually become tedious.
explanation: Because personal identity depends on specific causal circumstances, different policies lead to different people being born, so those who fare badly under a bad policy are not worse off than they would otherwise have been (they would not have existed at all), which is why person-affecting views struggle to locate a victim. Option A describes the separate problem of historical injustice. Denying bivalence belongs to logical fatalism, and the tedium worry is Williams on immortality, neither of which generates the non-identity problem.
